name: Layered silhouette stage with palette clock

source.description: Two inspected references stage stories on flat silhouette layers whose sky and palette change with time of day or life stage.

technique: Flat silhouette layers at different depths form a paper-theatre stage; a slow camera move gives parallax, and the palette (sky gradient, lights coming on) marks the passage of time, so time is told by colour rather than by text.
purpose: Atmosphere and the passage of time with cheap 2.5D depth; calm storytelling pace.
visual_behaviour: Hills, buildings and foreground as flat shapes; the sky shifts from warm to dark; windows and lamps light one by one; sun or moon travels an arc; the camera drifts.
mechanics: Depth-factored camera transforms; tweened CSS colour variables over several seconds; staggered light-ups; arc motion from two axes with different eases.

decomposition.timing: Palette shifts over 4-10 s; lights stagger 0.2-0.4 s; ref-910d9fc567 runs 57 s without a hard cut.

parameters.name: palette keyframes
parameters.description: Sky and ground colours per time of day

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: Pan and push over depth layers

failure_modes: Too many layers with detailed silhouettes slow the stage and clutter
Colour shift without a narrative reason

implementation.approach: No new code: Studio.space.camera over [data-depth] layers, GSAP tweens of CSS custom properties for the sky, Studio.draw.particles for stars, staggered fills for lights. This is the 'reuse an existing component' rung of the cost ladder.

measurements.value: 51.9 ms/frame median, 107.7 ms max, peak headless Chromium 313 MB

provenance.observed: Silhouette hills, house and figure on a paper-theatre stage; the sky moves through dusk and night; windows and a door light up.
Each life stage has its own palette (warm daylight, sunset, grey city, night).

evidence.notes: Dusk to night, parallax push, stars and lamp inspected.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown). The lighthouse scene is original.
